permanent.sub: Courses you can follow at any time, with a map to download.
permanent.text:
Permanent orienteering courses have been set up in a number of forests and country parks across the region. They provide an excellent opportunity to practise without the pressure of an event.

The controls are usually marked by a wooden post with a small red and white square.

Maps are either available to download from our website or purchase from a visitor's centre. The map shows all the controls, with suggested sequences to offer courses of differing lengths and levels of navigational difficulty.

kit.sub: Club clothing and how to get it.
kit.text:
SUFFOC members can purchase short and long sleeve running tops, vests and jackets supplied by Bryzos.

Fleeces, sweatshirts, hoodies, T-Shirts, polo shirts and wooly hats are also available.

Club orders for kit are put together at intervals, when there is enough demand.

If you're interested in a future order, please contact our Club Captain, Gareth Radcliffe, to register your interest and for further details.

safeguarding.sub: Who to talk to if you have a concern.
safeguarding.text: British Orienteering is committed to ensuring that everyone who participates in orienteering, including children and at-risk adults, has a positive experience in what can be a challenging environment, while keeping it as safe as possible. With this in mind, British Orienteering has continued to develop and implement policies and procedures which ensure everyone knows and accepts their responsibility for the duty of care owed to children and at-risk adults. Practical support for affiliated clubs such as SUFFOC includes providing a comprehensive safeguarding policy, along with training for our volunteer Welfare Officers and Coaches.
safeguarding.welfareText: If you have any concerns, however minor, please don’t hesitate to speak with one of our club welfare officers either at an event or by email:
